explicit_validation.explanation: The paper conducts direct validation by comparing BUS-GPT-3.5 and BUS-GPT-4 results against human evaluation using best-worst scaling (BWS) on the same 1,000 instances, analyzing alignment between automated question-answer metrics and human preferences.

prompts.notes: Exact prompts shown in Appendix Table 14; includes question-generation and answer-extraction instructions

guidelines.notes: Appendix Figure 4 shows detailed instructions; best-worst scaling with majority voting used to determine best/worst summary selections

sample_size.notes: All 1,000 test set updates used for both human BWS evaluation and BUS-GPT validation

quantitative_scores.notes: BUS-GPT-3.5 shows human backgrounds slightly outperform GPT-3.5 but underestimates GPT-3.5 quality compared to human evaluation
BUS-GPT-4 shows closer alignment with human best-worst scaling evaluation results
BUS-Human metric using human-generated QA pairs aligns well with human evaluation results

correlation_interpretation.interpretation: GPT-4 shows strong alignment, GPT-3.5 shows partial alignment
correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Relative comparison to BWS human evaluation results

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4-based BUS metric aligns well with human evaluation results, while GPT-3.5 shows discrepancies due to answer hallucination issues; human evaluation remains the gold standard for background summarization quality assessment.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation focuses on quantifiable answerability (BUS score), while human evaluation assesses comprehensive utility and contextual appropriateness
